transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-16
Start time: 16:00 UTC (Zoom)
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nadar (Product), Lena Park (Crestline), Ben O'Neill (Crestline), Sara Iqbal (Crestline), Tomás Ruiz (Crestline)

Summary:
Quick orientation of Redwood Console focusing on per-route usage analytics, how to map traffic to cost centers, and initial finops playbook for a 12-week pilot. Walkthrough includes Optimize recommendations (batching/quantization), brief security notes (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and next steps for a pilot run and benchmarks.

Topics covered:
- Per-route dashboards and tagging
- Cost decomposition (tokens, model variant, infra tier)
- Redwood Optimize suggestions and recommended knobs
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for 24/7 latency-sensitive flows
- Compliance and data residency basics

00:00 - 00:18 Speaker: Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, um Rafael will run through the console, i'll hop in for pricing and the pilot details, Priya from product is here to capture any feature asks.
00:19 - 00:40 Speaker: Lena Park: Thanks, Maya. We're excited. we're trying to get more visibility into how inference spend maps to our clinical pipelines — we have a mix of batched summarization jobs and real time chat for ops.
00:41 - 01:05 Speaker: Ben O'Neill: Yep, the main ask from platform is: how do we attribute cost to teams? we currently have a messy lambda that tags requests and we can't reconcile to infra bills.
01:06 - 01:30 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Great. so i'll share my screen, i'll start in the usage index, then show per-route dashboards, the route filter, and then the cost decomposition chart that slices by model variant, token class, and infra tier. apologies if the share is a little laggy.
01:31 - 02:05 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: (screen) Okay, so here is the console home. first, you can see traffic by route - we ingest tags from your headers, sdk keys, or our route mapping. if you don't have tags, you can map paths to routes in the routing table. we also support route-level metadata for owners and cost centers.
02:06 - 02:25 Speaker: Sara Iqbal: Wait, can owners map to internal chargeback codes? like our COA numbers?
02:26 - 02:46 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Yes, you can add arbitrary attributes — cost center, GCP project, COA — and then all dashboards will allow aggregation by that attribute. the export format includes a route->coa mapping for downstream billing.
02:47 - 03:15 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Here's a per-route timeline — you can pick a route and see tokens, calls, median latency, p95, model variant used, and infra tier. look at this: this route shows a spike in short seq chat requests around 02:00 UTC and a separate bulk summarization batch at 03:15.
03:16 - 03:44 Speaker: Lena Park: That's really helpful. does the console show cost per token or per call? we want both for different teams.
03:45 - 04:02 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: We show both. cost waterfall by route — token cost (model inference), infra cost (gpu time), and auxiliary (storage, logs). each is selectable. you can also run projections if you change batch sizes or quantization options.
04:03 - 04:30 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Now the cost decomposition view — here we break down cost by model variant (e.g. redwood-1.5b q4, redwood-7b fp16), then by route tag. notice the little "fallback" flag — when a higher-cost model was used as fallback, it shows separately so you can see fallback noise on costs.
04:31 - 04:58 Speaker: Ben O'Neill: That fallback flag would be great. sometimes we see spikes and can't tell if it's new traffic or fallback. can we set alerts on fallback rate?
04:59 - 05:25 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Yes, alerting and tracing hooks exist — you can hook SLOs and set alerts on fallback rate, median latency, and cost per minute. those alerts can call webhooks to pager or to your internal ticketing.
05:26 - 05:55 Speaker: Priya Nadar: Quick note: Optimize will suggest batch / cache / quant profiles per route. we'll show an example: for the summarization route, Optimize suggested batching up to 8 with prefix caching and q4_k on 7b which reduced cost per token by about 42% in similar workloads.
05:56 - 06:30 Speaker: Sara Iqbal: How aggressive are those quantization suggestions? we worry about regression in clinical outputs.
06:31 - 07:00 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Good question. Optimize ties recommendations to eval sets — you can run small evals and surface quality regressions. suggestions include an expected quality delta and a confidence score. we never change model for you automatically in a pilot unless you opt in.
07:01 - 07:30 Speaker: Tomás Ruiz: On compliance: can logs be forwarded to our SIEM and are audit logs tamper evident? we have strict audit requirements.
07:31 - 08:05 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Yes — for Private deployments you get full audit log retention in your VPC, and for Hosted we push structured logs to your syslog or to a customer's S3 with encryption. audit logs are signed and immutable for the retention period you choose; Tomás, i'll follow up with the SOC2 artifact and our KMS integration notes.
08:06 - 08:40 Speaker: Maya Chen: For the pilot contract we usually do a limited dedicated pool or hosted with committed throughput. for crestline's mixed profile (rt chat + batch summarization) i'd recommend a hybrid: hosted for dev and low-volume, dedicated reserved for production-critical chat route to hit latency SLO.
08:41 - 09:10 Speaker: Ben O'Neill: latencies — what's the expected p95 on dedicated vs hosted? we need p95 < 180ms for our chat path.
09:11 - 09:45 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Dedicated with pinned GPUs and small KV cache co-location can hit p95 around 120-160ms for 2k tokens typical. hosted varies by region and model: for same hardware profiles we'd expect 150-220ms. it depends on sequence length and batch tuning.
09:46 - 10:20 Speaker: Lena Park: Okay, so dedicated seems safer but more expensive. can the console simulate cost if we pin the chat route to dedicated and leave summarization on hosted?
10:21 - 10:55 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Yes — in the billing simulator you can create scenarios: route X on dedicated with N GPUs, route Y on hosted q4_k etc. it will output cost per month and per-1m calls and show unit cost delta.
10:56 - 11:30 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Another useful feature: ownership rollups. for crossover teams you can define attribution rules: e.g., 70% infra to product team, 30% to ml ops for shared endpoints. this feeds chargeback exports.
11:31 - 12:05 Speaker: Sara Iqbal: Can we tie routes to internal budgets so that when a route exceeds a spend threshold it auto-notifies the finance owner?
12:06 - 12:36 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Yep, spend rules — threshold alerts can trigger emails, webhooks, or even policy-based throttles (you can set soft caps).
12:37 - 13:05 Speaker: Ben O'Neill: On the tagging: we currently inject headers from the app. how brittle is the mapping? if a header is missing, what happens?
13:06 - 13:40 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: The router has fallback mapping logic; if headers missing we map by path patterns or IP ranges. we recommend SDK header injection to be deterministic. we also provide a small middleware snippet for common frameworks to ensure tags are applied.
13:41 - 14:20 Speaker: Priya Nadar: i'm going to point out a smaller workflow: you can save a route snapshot and then run a hypothetical "optimize" pass — it will apply recommended batching and show projected latency and cost impact. here i run it for their summarization pipeline — shows 37% cost drop, latency up 10% in median but within target.
14:21 - 14:55 Speaker: Lena Park: That projection is super useful to sell the idea internally. about quality: can we run A/B between fp16 and q4_k for a subset of traffic?
14:56 - 15:30 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Absolutely, you can do canary rollouts: route traffic split, canary evals on your test harness, and automatic rollback if quality metrics degrade beyond threshold. we also support function-calling and structured output checks in evals.
15:31 - 16:00 Speaker: Tomás Ruiz: For pilot data handling: does redact occur at the ingress? or do we keep raw request bodies in logs?
16:01 - 16:35 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: By default raw request bodies are retained in encrypted logs for X days; we can enable redaction at ingress and PII hashing. for Private installs the retention and storage is under your control. we'll include the retention config in the SOC2 pack.
16:36 - 17:10 Speaker: Maya Chen: ok, quick pricing note: pilot is typically a discounted committed amount for 90 days; if you go dedicated we arrange reserved GPU pricing tiers. i'll include a price sheet in the follow up.
17:11 - 17:45 Speaker: Sara Iqbal: On invoicing: do you support consolidated billing by cost center? we need the showback file to integrate with our ERP.
17:46 - 18:10 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Yes, exports can be CSV/flat JSON with COA mapping and consolidated invoices per cost center. integration with Netsuite/Workday is common; we also have S3 delivery for finance.
18:11 - 19:00 Speaker: Ben O'Neill: Let's talk about metrics we'd like during a pilot: tokens per call, median latency, p95, fallback rate, cost per 1k calls, and percent of traffic using cached prefixes.
19:01 - 20:00 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Good list. i'll make a template. also recommend a small synthetic benchmark we run on your sample traffic — we can share a runbook that shows how to simulate your seq length distribution.
20:01 - 21:00 Speaker: Lena Park: For the synthetic benchmark, can you run both hosted and dedicated so we can compare?
21:01 - 22:30 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Yes — we'll run both. for hosted tests we'll show average latencies across our regions; for dedicated tests we'll pin hardware and give you a p95 SLA expectation.
22:31 - 24:00 Speaker: Priya Nadar: one more product note — you can tag evals with prom-style labels, and tie regression alerts to prompt sets. that makes it easier to know if a model or quant change regresses a specific clinical prompt.
24:01 - 25:00 Speaker: Tomás Ruiz: Final security question for now: is there an option for hardware-backed key storage? we want HSM for key wraps.
25:01 - 25:40 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Yes — for Private and enterprise we integrate with customer HSM/KMS. for hosted customers we offer managed KMS and can support tenant-specific key management.
25:41 - 26:30 Speaker: Maya Chen: Great. real quick recap and next steps then we'll wrap.
26:31 - 27:30 Speaker: Maya Chen: Next steps: i'll send the pilot proposal and price worksheet; Rafael will share the benchmark runbook and an export of the per-route sample CSV; Tomás will send compliance questions. we'll target pilot kickoff week of 9/28.
27:31 - 29:00 Speaker: Sara Iqbal: sounds good. i want the pilot to include a finance-validated report each week so we can present to execs.
29:01 - 30:20 Speaker: Maya Chen: we can do weekly snapshot exports and a mid-pilot review.
30:21 - 31:00 Speaker: Ben O'Neill: a quick question — do you provide any pre-built Terraform or helm charts for Private installs?
31:01 - 32:10 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: We have terraform modules and helm charts, yes; for Private we usually do a joint runbook with your infra team. we'll share the repo links.
32:11 - 33:00 Speaker: Lena Park: any gotchas we should know about when taking a route to dedicated?
33:01 - 34:00 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: Main gotchas: cold KV caches at start causing a spike, mis-tagged traffic increasing a route's apparent cost, and model fallback config not tuned causing high cost. we usually recommend a warmup window and a pre-pilot shadow mode to validate traffic mapping.
34:01 - 35:00 Speaker: Priya Nadar: Also remember the preflight evals — run labeled prompt sets and check for quality regressions after any quant or model change.
35:01 - 36:30 Speaker: Tomás Ruiz: that warmup window: how long typically? we have 10M calls per day on a busy route so cache warm time matters.
36:31 - 37:05 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: usually 12-24 hours for prefix caches to reach steady state on high volume; for your high QPS route we might see stabilization in a few hours, but it depends on request diversity.
37:06 - 38:00 Speaker: Maya Chen: ok closing notes — we'll get the documents out. Rafael, anything else to add?
38:01 - 39:10 Speaker: Rafael Ortiz: i'll attach sample dashboards and a small explainer CSV. also sending a baseline config that you can import to your console. and i'll include a quick script to produce the traffic profile for the synthetic run.
39:11 - 40:00 Speaker: Lena Park: thanks — this was concise and useful. we'll review and get back on the stakeholder list.
40:01 - 41:00 Speaker: Sara Iqbal: thanks all. nice demo.
41:01 - 46:00 Speaker: (wrap up, informal chatter)
